land.text: Cebu island, where Legazpi founded the Villa del Santisimo Nombre de Jesus in 1565 after Rajah Tupas was overpowered

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps its Cebu row to 1571, the year Legazpi moved the capital to Manila.

capitals.name: Singhapala (Mabolo, Cebu City)
capitals.note: The page places Singhapala 'at what is now Mabolo, Cebu City'; the later Spanish settlement of 1565 is the same port. Coordinates approximate.

correction.text: the island of Cebu, in the rule of the rajahs of Singhapala, Sialo in the south and Nahalin in the north

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the infobox gives 'c. 1400-1565' while Cliopatria starts in 1497. The page also says the port-kingdom 'was founded as early as the 10th Century' and that a kingdom 'Suwu' appears in the 1225 Chinese Annals (an identification the page presumes); Chinese maritime logs of 1471-1588 show a shipping lane from Manila to Cebu. No extent is dated before 1521.

6,669 km2 (17 of the 18 cells of Cebu province), the island of Cebu with the offshore islands. The page gives no area; it names Sri Alho's Sialo (Carcar, Santander in the south) and Sri Ukob's Nahalin (Consolacion to Danao and Bantayan in the north), and Lapulapu's Mandawili (Mandaue) and Opon (Mactan) granted in Humabon's reign: all inside the island group the shape covers.

correction.text: the same island, shown only to 27 April 1565 when Legazpi landed and Rajah Tupas was overpowered

keyframe_review.note: The shape is right, its years are not: it runs to 1571 but the Hindu polity was dissolved by Legazpi's landing on 27 April 1565 ('Rajah Tupas challenged the Spaniards, but was overpowered'); from then the land is the Spanish colony.

region.text: the island of Cebu, the port-kingdom of Singhapala

ledger.note: c. 1400: the port-kingdom of Cebu appears (infobox 'c. 1400-1565'). The page says it 'was founded as early as the 10th Century' and credits Sri Lumay of Sumatra in legend; it gives no founding year.

region.text: Cebu, where the Spanish founded the Villa del Santisimo Nombre de Jesus

ledger.note: 27 April 1565: Legazpi lands at Cebu and overpowers Rajah Tupas. 'The expedition returned to Cebu and landed. Rajah Tupas challenged the Spaniards, but was overpowered'; the Spaniards 'founded a colony' there. The expedition had first anchored off Cebu on 13 February 1565.
1565: the Hindu polity of Cebu ends. 'The Hindu polity was dissolved during the reign of Rajah Tupas. Legazpi's forces ended it in the battle of Cebu in 1565.'

wars.name: Battle of Mactan
wars.outcome: Fought on 27 April 1521; Ferdinand Magellan was killed. No land changed hands: the Cebu rajahnate went on until 1565.
wars.note: The page ties Humabon and Lapulapu to the battle and records first Spanish contact in Humabon's reign; the rajah-by-rajah sides of the fight are not clear from the extract.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Cebu
wars.outcome: Legazpi anchored on 13 February 1565, landed on 27 April 1565 and overpowered Rajah Tupas; the Spaniards founded the Villa del Santisimo Nombre de Jesus and made Cebu the capital of the Spanish East Indies until the move to Manila in 1571.
wars.note: The page records no battle or bombardment, nor any treaty with Tupas (the blood compact of 16 March 1565 was with Datu Sikatuna of Bohol); the Cebu page calls it 'the battle of Cebu'.

certainty.note: A port polity on one island with named chiefs of the south and north; no survey line.

sources.title: Rajahnate of Cebu
sources.note: Identity, c. 1400 start, Singhapala, rajahs without years, Battle of Mactan 1521, end 1565.

sources.title: Miguel Lopez de Legazpi
sources.note: 13 February and 27 April 1565 at Cebu; Villa del Santisimo Nombre de Jesus; capital moved to Panay 1569 and Manila 1571.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Rajahnate of Cebu' 1497-1571 (two identical 6,669 km2 shapes): the island of Cebu and its offshore islands is right in place; the years are not. The infobox says c. 1400-1565 (the page also mentions a 10th-century foundation and a 1225 'Suwu'), the polity ended with Legazpi's landing on 27 April 1565, and Cliopatria's second shape runs to 1571 (the year Legazpi moved to Manila). One new keyframe covers 1400-1496.
Not settled: no reign years for the rajahs (Sri Lumay, Sri Bantug, Sri Parang, Humabon, Tupas) on the page, so no ruler strip; no dated vassal or tribute relation (a Siamese embassy 'paid tribute to Humabon' shortly before 1521, undated). The Legazpi page does not describe a battle, a bombardment or a treaty with Tupas. Mactan's ruler Lapulapu held Mandawili/Opon within the island group but is not a separate dossier.
Page budget: two pages, as allowed.
